title: The feel-good home
paragraphs: Our environments can affect the way we feel. This is not a new concept – after all, the traditional practice of feng shui has been with us for thousands of years. More recently, scientific research concluded that the design of healthcare environments could support patients in their recovery. Increasingly, however, it is our homes that are being seen as places we can improve our wellness.

A new approach to interior design suggests that many of us now care less about how our homes look and more about how they make us feel. How we feel can be influenced by a number of different things, including the furniture and objects within our homes and how these are arranged. For example, 'to create cosiness and the ability to connect with others, we want our furniture facing each other', says Lindsay T Graham, a personality and social psychologist. Smaller objects, too, have a lot of power, according to Monica Khemsurov, one of the founders of online design magazine Sight Unseen. Whether it's something an old friend made for us or a souvenir purchased while travelling, objects allow us to relive moments or feel closer to people we love at a glance. It makes sense, therefore, that taking a more intentional approach to where we place objects in our home, can affect our mood.

Other elements that help create a personal space that makes you feel good include the type of lighting, the use of colour and texture, as well as bringing nature into the home. Plants and 'natural materials, particularly unpainted wood, are really great for keeping our stress levels in check', says environmental psychologist Sally Augustin. And controlling stress levels can also be helped by making sure our work space and any clutter are hidden from sight when we want to feel calm, for example, during our night-time routine before going to bed.

However we choose to adjust our living spaces to improve wellness, the final tip from the experts is to not treat our homes as a museum. Instead, we should see them as idiosyncratic and constantly changing – just like us.

vocabulary.example: The layout of the house follows the principles of feng shui.
vocabulary.translation: 这座房子的布局遵循了风水原则。

vocabulary.example: The concept of sustainability has become very popular in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 可持续发展的概念近年来变得非常流行。

vocabulary.entry: **traditional practice** /trəˈdɪʃənl ˈpræktɪs/ 传统习俗；传统做法
vocabulary.example: This traditional practice has been passed down for hundreds of years.
vocabulary.translation: 这种传统做法已经传承了数百年。

vocabulary.example: Scientific research has shown that exercise is good for mental health.
vocabulary.translation: 科学研究表明运动对心理健康有益。

vocabulary.example: The study concluded that regular sleep improves memory.
vocabulary.translation: 这项研究得出结论，规律睡眠能提升记忆力。

vocabulary.example: A clean and quiet healthcare environment helps patients recover faster.
vocabulary.translation: 干净安静的医疗环境有助于患者更快康复。

vocabulary.example: He is still in hospital for recovery after the operation.
vocabulary.translation: 他手术后仍在医院进行康复治疗。

vocabulary.entry: **wellness** /ˈwelnəs/ n. 身心健康；健康状态
vocabulary.example: Yoga and meditation are great for your overall wellness.
vocabulary.translation: 瑜伽和冥想对整体身心健康很有好处。

vocabulary.example: She studied interior design at university and now runs her own studio.
vocabulary.translation: 她大学学的室内设计，现在经营着自己的工作室。

vocabulary.example: The soft blankets and warm lights add to the cosiness of the room.
vocabulary.translation: 柔软的毯子和暖灯增添了房间的温馨感。

vocabulary.example: You can talk to a psychologist if you feel anxious for a long time.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你长时间感到焦虑，可以找心理咨询师聊聊。

vocabulary.example: He is the founder of a well-known environmental protection organization.
vocabulary.translation: 他是一家知名环保组织的创始人。

vocabulary.example: I bought a small statue as a souvenir from my trip to Paris.
vocabulary.translation: 我从巴黎旅行回来买了一座小雕像当纪念品。

vocabulary.example: Looking at these photos makes me relive the happy times of my childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 看着这些照片，我仿佛重温了童年的快乐时光。

vocabulary.entry: **at a glance** /æt ə ɡlɑːns/ 一眼；立刻
vocabulary.example: He could tell at a glance that something was wrong.
vocabulary.translation: 他一眼就看出不对劲了。

vocabulary.entry: **intentional** /ɪnˈtenʃənl/ adj. 刻意的；有意的；有规划的
vocabulary.example: She made an intentional effort to spend more time with her family.
vocabulary.translation: 她刻意花更多时间陪伴家人。

vocabulary.example: A walk in the park can always improve my mood.
vocabulary.translation: 在公园散步总能改善我的心情。

vocabulary.example: Trust is a key element in a good relationship.
vocabulary.translation: 信任是良好关系的核心要素。

vocabulary.example: The soft lighting in the restaurant creates a romantic atmosphere.
vocabulary.translation: 餐厅里柔和的灯光营造出浪漫的氛围。

vocabulary.example: This silk fabric has a smooth and soft texture.
vocabulary.translation: 这种丝绸面料有着顺滑柔软的质感。

vocabulary.entry: **unpainted** /ʌnˈpeɪntɪd/ adj. 未上漆的；无涂层的
vocabulary.example: The room is decorated with unpainted wooden furniture for a natural look.
vocabulary.translation: 这个房间用未上漆的木质家具装饰，营造自然的风格。

vocabulary.entry: **keep sth in check** /kiːp ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɪn tʃek/ 控制住某事；抑制某事
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise helps keep your blood pressure in check.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动有助于控制血压。

vocabulary.example: I need to clear the clutter from my desk before I start working.
vocabulary.translation: 我开始工作前得先清理桌上的杂物。

vocabulary.entry: **night-time routine** /ˈnaɪt taɪm ruːˈtiːn/ 夜间常规流程；睡前流程
vocabulary.example: A relaxing night-time routine can help you sleep better.
vocabulary.translation: 一套放松的睡前流程能帮你睡得更好。

vocabulary.example: You can adjust the height of the chair to make it more comfortable.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以调整椅子的高度，让它更舒适。

vocabulary.entry: **living space** /ˈlɪvɪŋ speɪs/ 居住空间；生活空间
vocabulary.example: We want to make our living space more open and bright.
vocabulary.translation: 我们想让居住空间更开阔明亮。

vocabulary.entry: **idiosyncratic** /ˌɪdiəsɪŋˈkrætɪk/ adj. 独特的；有个人特色的
vocabulary.example: She has an idiosyncratic style of dressing that no one else can copy.
vocabulary.translation: 她有着别人无法模仿的独特穿搭风格。

vocabulary.example: The world is constantly changing, so we need to keep learning.
vocabulary.translation: 世界在不断变化，所以我们需要持续学习。

sentences.english: Our environments can affect the way we feel.
sentences.chinese: 我们所处的环境会影响我们的情绪。

sentences.english: This is not a new concept – after all, the traditional practice of feng shui has been with us for thousands of years.
sentences.chinese: 这并非一个全新的概念——毕竟，风水这一传统做法已经伴随我们数千年之久。

sentences.english: More recently, scientific research concluded that the design of healthcare environments could support patients in their recovery.
sentences.chinese: 近期，科学研究得出结论，医疗环境的设计能够辅助患者康复。

sentences.english: Increasingly, however, it is our homes that are being seen as places we can improve our wellness.
sentences.chinese: 而如今，我们的家也越来越被视作能够提升我们身心健康的场所。

sentences.english: A new approach to interior design suggests that many of us now care less about how our homes look and more about how they make us feel.
sentences.chinese: 一种全新的室内设计理念提出，如今我们中的许多人不再那么在意家的外观，反而更关注家带给我们的感受。

sentences.english: How we feel can be influenced by a number of different things, including the furniture and objects within our homes and how these are arranged.
sentences.chinese: 我们的情绪会受到诸多不同因素的影响，包括家中的家具和物品，以及它们的摆放方式。

sentences.english: For example, 'to create cosiness and the ability to connect with others, we want our furniture facing each other', says Lindsay T Graham, a personality and social psychologist.
sentences.chinese: 例如，人格与社会心理学家林赛·T·格雷厄姆说：“为了营造温馨感，创造与他人建立联结的氛围，我们会把家具面对面摆放。”

sentences.english: Smaller objects, too, have a lot of power, according to Monica Khemsurov, one of the founders of online design magazine Sight Unseen.
sentences.chinese: 线上设计杂志《未见之物》的创始人之一莫妮卡·凯姆苏罗夫认为，小摆件同样拥有巨大的力量。

sentences.english: Whether it's something an old friend made for us or a souvenir purchased while travelling, objects allow us to relive moments or feel closer to people we love at a glance.
sentences.chinese: 无论是老朋友为我们亲手做的物件，还是旅行时买的纪念品，这些物品都能让我们在一瞥之间重温过往时光，或是与所爱之人拉近距离。

sentences.english: It makes sense, therefore, that taking a more intentional approach to where we place objects in our home, can affect our mood.
sentences.chinese: 因此，更有目的性地摆放家中物品是明智的选择，因为这会影响我们的情绪。

sentences.english: Other elements that help create a personal space that makes you feel good include the type of lighting, the use of colour and texture, as well as bringing nature into the home.
sentences.chinese: 其他有助于打造令人愉悦的私人空间的要素，还包括灯光类型、色彩与材质的运用，以及将自然元素引入家中。

sentences.english: Plants and 'natural materials, particularly unpainted wood, are really great for keeping our stress levels in check', says environmental psychologist Sally Augustin.
sentences.chinese: 环境心理学家萨莉·奥古斯丁说：“绿植和天然材料，尤其是未上漆的木材，非常有助于控制我们的压力水平。”

sentences.english: And controlling stress levels can also be helped by making sure our work space and any clutter are hidden from sight when we want to feel calm, for example, during our night-time routine before going to bed.
sentences.chinese: 而当我们想要获得平静时，比如在睡前的夜间常规流程中，确保工作区域和所有杂物都不在视线范围内，也有助于我们控制压力水平。

sentences.english: However we choose to adjust our living spaces to improve wellness, the final tip from the experts is to not treat our homes as a museum.
sentences.chinese: 无论我们选择如何调整居住空间来提升身心健康，专家给出的最终建议是，不要把家当成一座博物馆。

sentences.english: Instead, we should see them as idiosyncratic and constantly changing – just like us.
sentences.chinese: 相反，我们应该把家看作是独具个人特色、且不断变化的空间——就像我们自己一样。
